text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Portugal sent Brussels plans to develop southern Alentejo region with the Alqueva dam a central element.
- European Commission authorises funding of 40 billion escudos for state airline TAP, the final tranche of planned state financing for its restructuring.
- Portugal's Inspector of Works considers Lusoponte bridge accident, in which at least four workers died, to be due to technical error.
- European parliament allows state oil company Petrogal further four years -- until 2004 -- to bring its petrol production into line with European fuel emission standards.

- The restructuring of electricity company EDP- Electricidade de Portugal, will continue after the first privatisation phase and the strategy to split the company into several parts will be reviewed, chairman Antonio de Almeida says.
- In 1996, 9.9 million tourists visited Portugal, spending 667 billion escudos. Portugal ranks 16th in the world as a tourist destination.
- After eight months, no company has yet completed the process of restructuring to win debt-relief under the terms of the so-called 'Mateus Plan'.
-Indicator measuring openness of Portuguese economy stood at 88.6 percent in 1995, a rise of 37 percent in the nine years since the country joined the European Union.
